overall: Tomorrow (Monday, July 6) in Atlanta is expected to start mostly sunny and warm before showers and thunderstorms develop likely after noon, with a 70% chance of precipitation. The NWS forecasts a high near 92°F with heat index values up to 98°F and southwest winds 0-10 mph. Afternoon convective activity driven by the approaching moisture surge will be the dominant story, potentially capping the daytime high as cloud cover and rain arrive.
forecast_obs_notes: Source model agreement is notably tight — all six models (ECMWF, GEM, GFS, HRRR, NBM, WEATHER_COM) point to 90-91°F as their top bucket, with expected TMAX values clustered between 89.3°F and 90.4°F; GFS has the highest confidence at 58% in that bucket. The full ensemble TMAX of 90.8°F sits slightly above the forecast-only model's 89.4°F, with yesterday's observed TMAX of 91.4°F providing upward support, but the strong afternoon storm threat introduces meaningful downside risk to the peak.
max_temp_prediction: The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets, with the model-derived top odd bucket at 87-88°F (29.1%) and second bucket at 89-90°F (22.9%); however, all source models center their expected TMAX around 89.3–90.4°F, making the 89-90°F odd bucket the most physically consistent target despite the raw probability edge to 87-88°F. The key uncertainty is timing of afternoon convection — an early storm could suppress the high into the upper 80s, while a delayed onset (post-peak heating) would allow a reach toward 90–91°F consistent with model means. Confidence is moderate (Tier 2, ~52% expected accuracy); the 89-90°F odd bucket appears the sharper value play given unanimous model clustering in the low-90s even-bucket range.
